articles.standfirst: Analizamos a 10 jóvenes promesas de 10 equipos (distintos) de fuera de LaLiga
articles.summary: Analizamos a 10 jóvenes promesas de 10 equipos (distintos) de fuera de LaLiga
articles.body: La Champions League se ha convertido, junto al Mundial, en el gran escaparate del 'planeta football'. Son muchos los jóvenes que cada temporada buscan dejar su sello. Por eso en MARCA, para celebrar el inicio de la temporada 2026-27, hemos querido seleccionar 10 promesas de fuera de LaLiga que pueden pegar el 'pelotazo' en la presente edición. Hemos escogido diez jugadores de 10 equipos diferentes para favorecer la diversidad, todos ellos nacidos a partir del 1 de enero de 2004. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 21 años. Altura: 1,85. Pie: Zurdo. El Como debuta... pero el hispano-argentino ya sabe, incluso, lo que es marcar en Champions. Se estrenó como goleador en 2023, con 19 años, en el triunfo del Real Madrid sobre el Nápoles (4-2). Ahora regresa convertido en la estrella de los de Cesc y con el aval que le otorgan los 20 goles y 17 asistencias que ha registrado en 78 partidos en el 'calcio'. "La construcción de nuestro juego está hecha para que le lleguen balones de una cierta manera en cada partido", asegura Cesc. En la frontal del área es letal. Atesora un disparo letal desde media distancia y una gran visión de juego. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 19 años. Altura: 1,68. Pie: Diestro. El 'niño bonito' del Oporto no encajaba en el esquema de Francesco Farioli y se vio obligado a abandonar Do Dragao. El jugador más joven (17 años y 7 meses) en marcar y asistir en un mismo partido con los 'dragones' puso rumbo a Roma previo pago de 25 millones. "Practica un fútbol que la gente adora", aseguraba su exentrenador Vítor Bruno. No es el más fuerte, pero cuenta con un centro de gravedad bajo que le hace terriblemente escurridizo. Gira bien, cambia de dirección fácil y acelera rápido. Le sobra elegancia... pero le falga continuidad. Demarcación: Central. Edad: 21 años. Altura: 1,90. Pie: Diestro. El ex del Rennes, fichado en enero previo pago de 63,6 millones de euros, se ha convertido en el acompañante de Van Dijk tras la salida de Konaté rumbo al Real Madrid. "Sé cuál es mi potencial", asegura Jacquet cuando le preguntan por las comparaciones con Saliba. Lanzado, en carrera, es un 'bisonte'. Cuenta con unas piernas larguísimas que le ayudan a robar fácil y una gran capacidad de salto que le hace difícil de superar en los duelos áreos. “Todavía es muy joven, creo que tiene todas las cualidades que necesitaremos para ese puesto", sostiene Andoni Iraola. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 18 años. Altura: 1,73. Pie: Zurdo. El Borussia Dortmund ha pagado 30 millones de euros al Genk por este clon de Arda Güler. El internacional griego atesora un 'guante' en la zurda. La pasada temporada, sin ir más lejos, registró tres goles y ¡18 asistencias! en 49 partidos. "Con su creatividad e inteligencia, enriquecerá nuestro equipo. Es muy habilidoso técnicamente y posee la capacidad de encontrar soluciones rápidas en espacios reducidos", subrayaba Ole Book, nuevo director deportivo del 'BVB', a modo de carta de presentación. "Es un auténtico '10' como los de antes", remarca su exentrenador Thorsten Fink. Demarcación: Extremo. Edad: 21 años. Altura: 1,76. Pie: Diestro. Un perfil muy diferente a Barcola. Al nuevo fichaje de Luis Enrique, llegado del Ajax a cambio de 45 millones de euros, ya le comparan en Bélgica con Eden Hazard: diestro, aunque suele actuar en izquierda; es habilidoso técnicamente, tiene salida por ambos perfiles... La Eredivisie se le quedaba pequeña: registró 17 goles y 15 asistencias en 44 partidos. "Algunos lo llaman arrogancia, pero Mika exuda confianza. Su regate es fantástico. Vuelve loco a todo el mundo. Mika, en forma, es una pesadilla para cualquier defensa", apunta su exentrenador Hans Somers. Demarcación: Portero. Edad: 21 años. Altura: 1,93. Pie: Diestro. Uno de los grandes 'culpables' de que el Lens haya conquistado Copa y Supercopa... y acabara segundo en la Ligue 1. No es de extrañar que Deschamps se lo llevara al Mundial. Risser responder al perfil de portero moderno. Muy espigado (1,93 metros), se encuentra cómodo bajo palos y se muestra muy consistente en los disparos a bocajarro. Es cierto que a menudo despeja más que bloca. "Es muy bueno en su línea, es bueno gestionando la profundidad, es bueno con los pies y también es bueno saliendo de su línea en los balones aéreos", indica su exentrenador Pierre Sage. Demarcación: Medio. Edad: 20 años. Altura: 1,82. Pie: Diestro. El ex del Friburgo, fichado a cambio de 60 millones de euros, viene de ser elegido 'Mejor Jugador Joven' de la Europa League y de erigirse en una de las revelaciones del Mundial. Manzambi, autor de siete goles y nueve asistencias la temporada pasada, destaca por su descomunal despligue. Puede jugar en cualquier posición del eje central (pivote, mediocentro, interior, mediapunta...) o tirado a la izquierda. "Es un futbolista callejero, de esos que necesitan libertad. Ya lo habéis visto: puede presionar, tiene buena habilidad para el regate y sabe definir”, asegura Murat Yakin. En el último tramo de curso desarrolló, sobre todo, su capacidad de llegada. Demarcación: Medio. Edad: 18 años. Altura: 1,85. Pie: Diestro. El '6' de Marruecos fue el primer gran nombre propio del Mundial. "Me impresionó muchísimo. ¡Cómo juega el muchacho! Apenas 18 años y mucho fútbol. Estaba en todas partes del campo, moviéndose, creando jugadas, desarmando. Si continúa así, este chico llegará lejos", aseguró Romário tras el 1-1 ante Brasil. Por el momento, ha llegado al Manchester City, que ha pagado 95 millones al Lille para convertirle en el mayor traspaso al extranjero en la historia de la Ligue 1. Todocampista. Recuerda por planta -mide 1,86 metros- y físico a Guendouzi. Le gusta 'verticalizar' el juego, aunque debe comenzar a 'producir' números. Con los 'dogos' no marcó. Sólo registró cuatro asistencias en 96 partidos. Demarcación: Extremo. Edad: 18 años. Altura: 1,68. Pie: Zurdo. El canterano del Bayern es tan joven que ni siquiera ha sido incluido en la lista 'A' para la Champions. La pasada temporada ya dejó su sello. Sólo Lamine Yamal (10) le superaba en goles producidos en Liga de Campeones (4) antes de cumplir 18 años. Creció admirando a Odegaard mientras se 'pulía' como mediapunta, pero brilla, también, jugando de extremo a pierna cambiada. "Soy muy rápido en los primeros metros, me gustan los 1 contra 1 y tengo remate. Mido algo menos de 1,70 metros, no soy el más alto, pero mi bajo centro de gravedad me ayuda a regatear", asegura el propio Karl. Demarcación: Medio. Edad: 20 años. Altura: 1,87. Pie: Diestro. Su condición de 'box-to-box' -cuenta con un gran ida y vuelta- le convierte en un futbolista ideal para Farioli. Tiene piernas para garantizar la presión adelantada y las carreras a alta intensidad que exige el 'futebol' del Oporto. No sólo roba. También llega. La pasada temporada, sin ir más lejos, registró ocho dianas y siete asistencias. "Técnicamente es donde más puedo mejorar. Si logro desarrollar esto, podré usar mi fuerza, capacidad de intercepción y control del balón a larga distancia para generar peligro, crear ocasiones y marcar goles", apunta Froholdt. "Tiene un 'motor' increíble. Es capaz de repetir acciones a alta intensidad, esto es algo único", subraya Farioli.

articles.title: Cata Coll, nominada a mejor portera en el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: Comparte terna con la alemana Ann-Katrin Berger, la inglesa Hannah Hampton, la brasileña Lorena y la japonesa Ayaka Yamashita
articles.summary: Comparte terna con la alemana Ann-Katrin Berger, la inglesa Hannah Hampton, la brasileña Lorena y la japonesa Ayaka Yamashita
articles.body: Ya están sobre la mesa las cinco candidatas al Trofeo Yashin femenino, el premio a la mejor portera del año dentro de la gala del Balón de Oro, y España vuelve a tener representación de lujo: Cata Coll comparte terna con la alemana Ann-Katrin Berger, la inglesa Hannah Hampton, la brasileña Lorena y la japonesa Ayaka Yamashita. El argumento central de su candidatura es la Champions League. Coll fue una pieza clave en el camino del Barça hacia su cuarto título continental, cerrado con un contundente 4-0 al Lyon en la final, y llegó a ese partido después de una racha de porterías a cero que la consolidó como una de las guardametas más sólidas de Europa durante el tramo decisivo de la competición. A eso se suma su rendimiento en la Liga F, donde ha sido titular fija de un Barça dominante, y la confianza que el club le mostró en octubre al renovarle el contrato hasta 2029, blindando su portería a largo plazo.

articles.title: From jail to football redemption to royal crown: Who is UK-raised goalkeeper George Kamurasi, set to become a king in Uganda?
articles.summary: Football News: What began as a troubled teenage life, followed by a second chance through football, has now taken George Desmond Kamurasi to a destination few could .
articles.body: What began as a troubled teenage life, followed by a second chance through football, has now taken George Desmond Kamurasi to a destination few could have imagined — the throne of Uganda’s historic Tooro Kingdom.At 36, Kamurasi is still better known around south-east London as “Big G”, the towering goalkeeper and captain of non-league side SE Dons. He plays in the ninth tier of the English football pyramid, gives fiery team talks, coaches young players and has built a family life in Britain.But this week, the football pitch suddenly became a long way from the biggest stage awaiting him.Kamurasi has been selected by the Tooro Royal Succession Committee to succeed his late cousin, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who died in the United States aged 34 after receiving treatment for cancer. Fifteen of the 18 committee members present at a September 4 meeting backed Kamurasi, according to journalist Andrew Mwenda. The 21-member committee was formed by the Babiito royal clan to guide the succession process.His formal proclamation, however, is still to come. Tooro custom requires the public announcement of the new monarch after King Oyo’s burial, which is scheduled for September 12.For Kamurasi, the extraordinary turn of events has transformed a man who once spoke about simply trying to rebuild his life into a potential king.‘I was angry’: The teenage years that changed everythingLong before the royal succession committee came calling, Kamurasi was dealing with a very different kind of battle.He has spoken publicly about losing his mother when he was 14 and falling into what he described as the wrong circle. His teenage years spiralled badly enough for him to spend time in jail.In a recollection quoted by Pulse Uganda, Kamurasi said the experience forced him to confront his own choices.“I was in that cell when I realised that everything I had done was my fault. I took responsibility,” he said.That moment became a turning point.Instead of allowing his mistakes to define him, Kamurasi threw himself into football. The sport offered something that his life had been missing — structure, ambition and a reason to keep moving.“I came out; went into football and put myself out there. I chased it and won things,” he recalled.His journey even took him into the orbit of the Nike Academy. Kamurasi has recalled being scouted and later playing in Barcelona while Pep Guardiola was watching.“Things that were not possible. I wanted it more than anything else,” he said.For someone who had once found himself sitting in a prison cell as a teenager, football became far more than a game. It became his route back.From goalkeeper to coach, captain and mentorKamurasi never became a household name in professional football, but he carved out a place for himself in England’s sprawling non-league game.He has been associated with several lower-league clubs and has worked as a goalkeeper and coach. Football records and profiles have linked him with clubs including Ashford United, while his goalkeeping work has included spells with other non-league sides.Standing around 6ft 6in, Kamurasi became a distinctive figure between the posts. But his influence increasingly extended beyond saving shots.At SE Dons, his leadership has become part of his identity.The south-east London club, based around Bexleyheath and the surrounding area, has developed a strong social-media following and become one of the better-known media-driven grassroots football clubs in England. The club’s rise has taken it from Sunday-league football into the Southern Counties East Football League Premier Division, the ninth level of the English pyramid.Kamurasi has become one of its central figures.Videos from the club show the goalkeeper delivering passionate, sometimes uncompromising team talks. His message is familiar: take responsibility, work harder, recover from mistakes and do not allow setbacks to decide who you become.It is a philosophy that appears to have been forged by his own life.The boy who once needed football to find direction eventually became the man using football to give direction to others.And now he could be expected to do the same on a much larger stage.A football captain with a royal bloodlineThe surprise surrounding Kamurasi's selection comes partly from how ordinary his adult life in Britain has appeared.But the connection to the Tooro throne is deeply rooted.Kamurasi was born in Uganda and is a member of the Babiito royal family. He is the son of George Desmond “Jimmy” Mugenyi, who was the younger brother of King Patrick David Mathew Olimi Kaboyo III, King Oyo’s father.That makes Kamurasi a first cousin of the late king.His grandfather was King George Rukidi III, who ruled Tooro from 1928 to 1965. The family’s historical links with Britain run particularly deep: Rukidi III welcomed Queen Elizabeth II during her 1954 visit to Uganda.According to the succession account released after the committee meeting, the line of succession was also supported by the late Rukidi III’s will, which placed Kamurasi’s father in the succession line behind his elder brother.So while Kamurasi may look like an unlikely king from the perspective of a London football pitch, his selection is rooted in a longstanding royal lineage.From King Oyo’s shadow to an unexpected successorThe succession became necessary after the death of King Oyo, whose own story was extraordinary.Oyo became Tooro’s monarch in 1995 at just three years old following the death of his father. He subsequently became internationally known as the world’s youngest reigning monarch.His death at 34 brought a period of uncertainty to the kingdom.The late king’s funeral is scheduled for September 12, marking the end of a nine-day period of mourning. The date is particularly symbolic because it falls on what would have been the 31st anniversary of Oyo’s coronation. His remains were returned to Uganda on September 4 and taken to Karuziika Palace in Fort Portal, where they have been lying in state.The succession process has not been entirely free of competing claims and questions, including reports surrounding whether Oyo had a biological heir. But the Royal Succession Committee has now backed Kamurasi, with the formal cultural process still to be completed.The reported choice has also received support from senior Ugandan officials, according to accounts of the succession process, with the committee saying the decision was consistent with Tooro customs and succession precedent.‘Big G’ faces the biggest decision of his lifeFor all the excitement surrounding the selection, the biggest question may be whether Kamurasi actually wants the life that comes with it.British media reports have described him as reluctant to leave London. He is married to a British woman and has a young son, and his life has been built around his family and football.The Times and The Sun have both highlighted the extraordinary contrast between his current existence as a non-league footballer and the responsibilities of becoming Omukama of Tooro.There are also questions within Uganda about whether someone who spent much of his adult life in Britain can adequately represent the Tooro people. Others, however, have pointed to the qualities that have made him a leader in football — his directness, discipline and no-nonsense personality — as potential strengths.And in perhaps the most surreal detail of all, Kamurasi could even miss the funeral of the cousin he is set to succeed. His football commitments reportedly clash with the upcoming cup fixture for SE Dons.That detail captures the strange crossroads at which Kamurasi now finds himself.One part of his life is waiting in a London football dressing room. Another is waiting at a royal palace thousands of miles away.The goalkeeper who found purpose could now have a kingdom to leadFor years, Kamurasi's story was about escaping his past.He went from losing his mother as a teenager, falling into trouble and spending time in jail to discovering purpose through football. He chased opportunities, played the game, became a goalkeeper and eventually a coach and captain — turning the lessons of his own difficult adolescence into messages for younger players.Now, those same qualities are being viewed through an entirely different lens.Resilience. Accountability. Leadership. Discipline.They were once simply the tools he needed to rebuild himself. They may soon become the qualities expected of a king.Kamurasi has not yet formally been proclaimed Omukama. That moment is expected only after King Oyo’s burial, in accordance with Tooro tradition. But the extraordinary possibility is already here.The man known in south-east London as “Big G” — a goalkeeper whose biggest concern might ordinarily be keeping a clean sheet — has suddenly been placed on the path to a royal crown.And if his football journey taught him anything, it is that a difficult past does not have to dictate the future.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Scott McTominay heart procedure 'a complete success'
articles.summary: Napoli say Scott McTominay's heart surgery "was a complete success" and expect the Scotland midfielder to resume training this month.
articles.body:
Napoli have said Scott McTominay's heart surgery "was a complete success" and expect the Scotland midfielder to resume training this month.

The 29-year-old's ablation procedure - a minimally invasive operation to correct irregular heart rhythms - took place at Spire Manchester Hospital on Tuesday morning.

McTominay was substituted after 56 minutes of Napoli's 2-1 Serie A defeat by Como on 30 August.

A mild benign arrhythmia was discovered, prompting the corrective treatment.

Napoli, who said in statement , external that "McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training", had expected the former Manchester United player to return to action after the international break in early October.

When his heart issue was announced, McTominay posted on Instagram: "See you soon Napoli. I won't take long."

Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games as Scotland head coach - home and away against Slovenia as well as matches with North Macedonia and Switzerland in the Nations League - are scheduled for the end of September and early October.

According to the NHS, , external an arrhythmia is when the heart beats too quickly or too slowly, or the heartbeat is not steady.

The British Heart Foundation explains , external a cardiac arrhythmia ablation involves using heat or cold energy to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

articles.title: Calendario del Betis en la Champions League: partidos en casa y fuera, fechas, horarios y rivales
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos ya conocen fechas y horarios de sus partidos de la Fase de Liga
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos ya conocen fechas y horarios de sus partidos de la Fase de Liga
articles.body: La UEFA publicaba hace un par de semanas las fechas y horarios de los partidos correspondientes a las ocho jornadas de la Fase de Liga de la Champions League, que arranca en septiembre y se prolongará hasta finales de enero. Una agenda en la que el Betis comienza jugando fuera de casa, frente al Lille, en Francia, y cierra también a domicilio, visitando en Alemania al Bayern de Munich, en el Allianz Arena. Después de visitar al Lille el martes 8 de septiembre, el primer partido de la competición en el Estadio de La Cartuja será el miércoles 14 de octubre frente al Oporto. Los de Pellegrini repetirán en casa el miércoles 21 de octubre ante el Feyenoord y alcanzarán el ecuador de esta primera etapa del torneo estrella de la UEFA viajando a Alemania para enfrentarse al Borussia Dortmund el miércoles 4 de noviembre. Estos cuatro primeros encuentros se jugarán desde las 21.00 horas. También a esa hora, el martes 24 de noviembre, los verdiblancos jugarán en Eslovaquia ante el Slovan Bratislava. Su único partido en el horario de tarde, desde las 18.45 horas, será el que jueguen el miércoles 9 de diciembre en casa ante el Como italiano. Y para cerrar la Fase de Liga, los dos rivales más duros de su calendario: el miércoles 20 de enero a las 21.00 horas en La Cartuja frente al campeón de la Premier League, el Arsenal, y el miércoles 27 de enero, en ese mismo horario, en el Allianz Arena frente al campeón de la Bundesliga, el Bayern de Munich. La visita al Lille, el partido en casa ante el Oporto y el duelo también en La Cartuja ante el Feyenoord, en el primer mes y medio de competición, pueden marcar la trayectoria de los de Pellegrini en esta Champions. Cerrar la Fase de Liga ante los dos adversarios del primer bombo del sorteo, a la larga, puede resultar beneficioso para los verdiblancos si ambos hacen los deberes antes de final de año y llegan a las jornadas finales sin urgencias, aunque con el nuevo formato de la competición, cada punto suele ser clave en los cruces y el orden de las eliminatorias.

articles.title: Ander Herrera, primera alegría y una pena con el Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: El capitán celebró su primer triunfo tras su vuelta pero falló un penalti
articles.summary: El capitán celebró su primer triunfo tras su vuelta pero falló un penalti
articles.body: Ander Herrera vivió una noche de contrastes contra el Antequera. Celebró su primera victoria tras su regreso al Real Zaragoza pero falló una pena máxima que pudo costar dos puntos al equipo si no marca en el descuento Edu Espiau. Ese tanto alivió al capitán y pudo dejar ese error en un segundo plano. El centrocampista no está acostumbrado a lanzar los penaltis. Sin embargo, tomó la responsabilidad ante la sorpresa de muchos y su lanzamiento se estrelló en el poste y en las piernas y espalda del portero. Tenía ganas de gritar su primer gol pero la fortuna no estuvo de su lado. Habrá que ver si el siguiente lo vuelve a tirar o se cambia de lanzador. La parte positiva, además del triunfo, es que físicamente se le está viendo bien. Había dudas por su historial de lesiones en los últimos años, pero en este inicio ha disputado casi el 100% de los minutos y a sus 37 años ha demostrado un buen estado de forma en estas dos primeras jornadas. Eso sí, el centro del campo no termina de funcionar e Ibai Gómez podría cambiar su pareja en la medular. De momento, está siendo Terrer y muchos están pidiendo a Rubén Díez, quien de momento apenas ha jugado ocho minutos cuando llegó siendo uno de los fichajes más destacados.

articles.title: Liverpool announce five-year shirt sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines
articles.summary: The deal is reportedly worth more than $405m, which would place it among the most lucrative in the Premier League.
articles.body:
Liverpool have ‌agreed a five-year deal for Turkish Airlines to ⁠become their ⁠main club partner from June 1, 2027, which means the first change in the Anfield side’s ⁠leading shirt sponsor since 2010, ending a 17-year run for Standard Chartered.

The deal announced on Tuesday will ⁠be worth in excess of 300 million pounds ($405.78m) according to media reports, which would place it among the most lucrative in the Premier League.

While the precise figures have not been ‌confirmed, it is likely to match the income from Manchester United’s shirt sponsorship deal with Qualcomm, which was signed in August 2024.

Standard Chartered will remain affiliated with Liverpool as a Global Partner, said a club statement, but Turkish Airlines will take the primary position ⁠in Liverpool’s branding.

“The front of the ⁠Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club,” said Liverpool’s chief commercial officer Ben Latty.

“Turkish Airlines is a globally ⁠recognised organisation with an extensive international network and we look forward to beginning ⁠our partnership and building a strong ⁠relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005,” he added, referring to Liverpool’s Champions League final comeback ‌win in Istanbul.

The deal adds to a growing sponsorship portfolio within football for Turkish Airlines, who are an ‌official ‌partner of the Champions League and main sponsor of Turkiye’s national team.

In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than 700 million pounds ($950m) for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League.

Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

articles.title: Liverpool news: Alexis Mac Allister 'sad' at no new Liverpool contract offer
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister says he is "very sad" not to have been offered a new deal by the club and had "options" to leave in the summer.
articles.body:
Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister says he is "very sad" not to have been offered a new deal by the club and had "options" to leave in the summer.

The Argentine, who joined on a five-year contract from Brighton in June 2023, saw team-mates Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch extend their Reds deals this year.

Speaking before Liverpool 's Champions League game against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday, Mac Allister spoke openly about his future at the club.

"I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad," said the 27-year-old.

"Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

"I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it.

"At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I didn't get mine. Of course, there is still time.

"The fans don't need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here."

Mac Allister, who has been linked with a move to Manchester City , explained he had not had direct contact with Liverpool over the decision not to extend his deal.

"We won a Premier League together, we went through difficult times together and I always give my best so we will see what happens," said Mac Allister, who helped Argentina win the 2022 World Cup.

"I don't think I have to prove something - but I have to show the level I can perform and, hopefully, that's the case.

"I love this club. I love the fans. I know very well this is an amazing club and this city has something very special. I love being here."

He added: "There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I'm in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club."

Mac Allister was a key part of the Liverpool side that won the Premier League title in 2024-25, but admitted "it wasn't a good season for me individually and for us as a team" as the Reds finished fifth last season and sacked manager Arne Slot.

He made 55 appearances last season for Liverpool , an increase on the 49 games he played in 2024-25.

Andoni Iraola was appointed this summer as Slot's successor and, after using Mac Allister as a substitute in the top-flight opener at Newcastle , has started him in the past two games.

Speaking about Mac Allister's contract, the Spaniard said: "We all have personal situations with different contracts.

"The important thing is he wants to be here. We haven't been together a long time but he has been an important player and I rate him very highly.

"There is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations."

Asked about Iraola, Mac Allister said: "Since I came to pre-season and worked under Andoni, I could see something special.

"He is a really good coach, he knows very well what he wants to do and we are trying to get there.

"I've not had any conversations with him about [the contract]. But when I see the way he wants us to play and the way we train, I think this can be a successful year."

This wasn't quite Mohamed Salah in a mixed zone saying he was "more out than in" , but it was certainly a shock to hear Alexis Mac Allister speak so candidly in such a public setting so early in the season.

The Argentine still has almost two years left on his current contract, but it has clearly not gone unnoticed that both Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch signed new long-term deals this year.

Perhaps Mac Allister's comments are a strategy to see the reaction from the fanbase, but, deep down, he will know he must return to the levels he showed during Liverpool 's title-winning campaign in 2024-25 when he scored five goals and provided five assists.

Richard Hughes - the now former Liverpool sporting director - was involved in the discussions with Mac Allister's camp and BBC Sport understands the Reds hierarchy opted not to offer him a new deal after a below-par campaign last term.

Liverpool will have a new sporting director in the near future and, although Mac Allister was adamant he has nothing to prove, there will surely be an added desire on his part to show his quality.

If he can do that, then there is every chance there could be another chapter to Liverpool and Mac Allister's relationship.

Now it remains to be seen how another contract saga - something Liverpool are getting increasingly used to - plays out over the course of the season.

articles.title: Alexis Mac Allister: Liverpool midfielder 'very sad' over no new contract and admits he could have left in summer
articles.summary: Alexis Mac Allister 'very sad' at not being offered new Liverpool contract; 27-year-old midfielder has two years left on Anfield deal; team-mates Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch signed new long-term contracts this year
articles.body:
The 27-year-old confirmed he has two years left on his Reds deal, which he signed when he joined the club in the summer of 2023.

The Argentina international's unhappiness comes after fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch penned new long-term contracts this year.

Speaking ahead of Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid, Mac Allister told a pre-match press conference: "There was a chance [he could have left the club in the summer].

"As everyone knows, I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which makes me very, very sad.

"Everyone can see I give my 100 per cent for this football club, every single day in training and games. Of course I can have very good games, very bad games like everyone. I always give my best.

"And I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts, and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I didn't get mine.

"Of course, there is still time. The fans don't need to worry because I will give my 100 per cent until the last day I'm here.

"We will see what happens. There were options to leave this summer, and I think right now I'm in the right club and I have the mindset to give my 100 per cent for this club."

Questioned whether talks were ongoing over a new contract, he replied: "Maybe. I don't know. It's going to depend on how I perform during this year. They are right to make the decision as well, but hopefully they change their minds."

Asked whether he was given a reason for no new contract, he said: "Not really. There wasn't any direct conversation with me - it was with my agent.

"I don't want to say things they never said, but what I got from my agent was that they were not in a position to renew me.

"It's really sad because we won a Premier League together, we've been through difficult times together, and I always give my best. We will see what happens, but of course it makes me a little bit sad."

Mac Allister was linked with a move to Manchester City this summer.

Questioned on why he did not leave Anfield, he replied: "Because this is the right club. I love being here, and this is something special."

He added: "I love this club, I love being here, I love the fans.

"As a player, you can be at a club for a long, long time and you don't really realise where you are - that doesn't happen to me.

"I know very well that this is an amazing club, that this city has something very special and I love being here."

'I've not spoken with Iraola over new deal'

Mac Allister has started in Liverpool's last two league games, which saw them draw at home to Nottingham Forest and then win at Ipswich to help give new Reds boss Andoni Iraola an unbeaten start.

But Mac Allister revealed he has not spoken about his future with the Spaniard, whom he had plenty of praise for.

"Definitely since I've come to pre-season and I worked under Andoni, I could see something special," he said.

"He's a really good coach. He knows very well what he wants to do, and we are trying to get there.

"I haven't had any conversations with him about it.

"When I see the way he wants us to play and train, I think this can be a successful season so that's why I think this is the right club and the right moment to be here."

Iraola called Mac Allister an "important" player and says there is still time for his contract situation to be resolved.

He told a press conference: "We all have personal situations with different contracts. The important thing is he wants to be here and continue here.

"We haven't been together a long time but he has been an important player and I rate him very highly.

"Definitely there is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations."

He added: "I am very happy with his performances - he played really well on Friday [at Ipswich] and I hope I can help him to still improve.

"He is very experienced player who has already achieved massive things, but I hope I can help him in his development as a player and then everything goes well then those problems will definitely be solved".

Mac Allister was a key part of Liverpool's 2024/25 Premier League title, having also won the Carabao Cup the season before.

Asked whether he has anything to prove this season amid doubts over a new deal, the 2022 World Cup winner replied: "Not really because I'm always the same guy and player, and I'm not going to change.

"I think in these three years at the club I've done very good things. We went through difficult times; we went through a lot of things. We won a Premier League, we won a Carabao Cup, so for me it's a very successful period of my life.

"I don't think I have to prove something, but of course I have to show the level that I can perform, and hopefully that's the case."

Mac Allister's overall quality ratings have dipped season on season since he joined Liverpool in the summer of 2023, according to data provider Gradient .

Gradient rates each metric according to the quality of a player's actions, rather than simply the quantity of them.

In terms of quantity, per 90 minutes, Opta data also points to a decline in Mac Allister's output. Ratings out of 100 show his percentile rank among midfielders across Europe's top five leagues.

The most striking change has been in his defensive output. Mac Allister has gone from ranking among Europe's elite midfielders in several defensive metrics to sitting towards the bottom of that group.

What next for Mac Allister after contract admission?

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Vinny O'Connor:

"No scapegoating, no talk of anyone being thrown under the bus - just genuine upset that he's the odd one out.

"Alexis Mac Allister is the only one of Liverpool's 'first-choice' title-winning midfield trio from 2025 to be told the club is not in a position to offer new terms.

In the last six months, Ryan Gravenberch has signed up until 2032 while Dominik Szoboszlai has committed until 2031.

"Mac Allister says he's happy for them, they deserve it, but, reading between the lines, he's asking the question as to why is there nothing on the table for him?

"There's an irony that he was speaking before facing Atletico Madrid, one of the sides he's been linked with. There was also talk during the summer window of interest from Manchester City.

"He freely admitted he could have gone. There were opportunities. But, he stayed because Liverpool, in his mind, remains the right club for him and one that he is fully committed to, whatever the contract situation.

"Last season wasn't his best and there is an argument to say there is a sensibility about the decision taken on football reasons.

"So is this the beginning of the end of his time at Anfield?

"Not necessarily. In his manager's words: "There is still a lot of time to talk about these contract situations."

"Mac Allister's own take is that things can change, along with an admission he has to show the level at which he can perform.

"That is not necessarily a bad thing for Iraola, having a player of Mac Allister's quality with the added motivation of proving his worth.

"And, just as the tone was different to Mo Salah at Leeds last season - even if the openness with which Mac Allister spoke was no less surprising - it feels a similar outcome is far from set in stone at this stage.

"Yes, there was surprise in the room, but maybe we're not in for another drawn out transfer saga."

articles.title: Fifa: Legal action against world football's governing body to include women's schedule
articles.summary: Legal action from the top European leagues and global players' union Fifpro against Fifa is extended to include the world governing body's "abusive conduct" towards the women's game.
articles.body:
Legal action from the top European leagues and global players' union Fifpro against Fifa has been extended to include the world governing body's "abusive conduct" towards the women's game.

European Leagues, which represents 53 professional divisions, including the Premier League, and 1,328 clubs in 34 countries, first filed the complaint to the European Commission to protect the welfare of men's players in October 2024.

The complaint stated that Fifa abused a dominant position under European competition law allegedly by not including national leagues and player unions over the new men's international calendar announced in 2023.

In a statement on Tuesday, it said it is extending the scope of its complaint to include "Fifa's abusive conduct regarding the women's international match calendar and related women's football regulatory decisions".

"Fifa's conduct threatens the growth and financial sustainability of women's professional leagues, and risks player health and wellbeing," European Leagues said.

"The European Commission must now act to ensure that EU law is respected and that the future of women's professional football is not determined unilaterally by Fifa.

"The submission details the same pattern of conduct identified in the original complaint - Fifa holds conflicting roles as governing body and competition organiser, which gives rise to a conflict of interest.

"As in men's football, Fifa consistently uses its regulatory power to favour its own competition and commercial interests to the detriment of women's football and of European national leagues."

European Leagues welcomed 14 women's divisions to its ranks in June, including the Women's Super League and the Scottish Women's Premier League.

It also includes the Premier League, English Football League, Scottish Professional Football League, La Liga, Serie A and the Bundesliga.

A Fifa spokesperson said: "Fifa believes in the power of dialogue as opposed to legal action and escalation, and our doors always remain open to reach agreements in the best interest of football.

"As a matter of fact, a landmark agreement reached with Fifpro earlier this year enabled groundbreaking reforms to the global transfer system, jointly adopted in full consensus with all football stakeholders.

"As the women's global landscape continues to grow and broaden, Fifa is committed to expand and identify emerging stakeholders in anticipation of the conversations that will begin on the next iteration of the March calendar."

Fifa president Infantino will stand for re-election

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Fifa has been under intense scrutiny in the summer after its president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and its other competitions to private investors.

Infantino's plan sparked a global outcry, with Uefa threatening to boycott all Fifa competitions , including the World Cup.

European football's governing body dropped the threat after receiving assurances from Fifa that the plan will not go ahead.

Infantino has been under pressure from several confederations after the scrapped Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan but the Swiss is set to stand for re-election as president in March.

The 56-year-old, who first became president in 2016, is seeking a third term in the role until 2031.

Fifa last week accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership", in a challenge to litigation over Infantino's plan.

Uefa had filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

articles.title: Lawrence Shankland: Rangers captain & Scotland forward out for up to four months and may need surgery
articles.summary: Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland will be out for up to four months because of a hamstring tear and the Scotland forward may have surgery.
articles.body:
Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland will be out for up to four months because of a hamstring tear and the forward may have surgery.

Speaking before Wednesday's Scottish Premiership visit of St Mirren, manager Derek McInnes confirmed his 31-year-old skipper had suffered a recurrence of the injury when both were at Hearts last season. Shankland missed nine weeks.

He has scored four goals in 10 Rangers appearances so far this term but came off early in Saturday's 1-0 home league win over Motherwell. His replacement, Ryan Naderi, scored the game's only goal.

"He's had a tear, it's a 2cm tear in his hamstring so similar, very similar to the one he did previously at Hearts in January," McInnes said.

"He's actually in London now, he's getting an ultrasound scan, a follow-up scan which is just to determine with the specialist whether he has surgery or whether we just let that heal naturally, as it did the last time.

"If he has the surgery then he might be an extra three or four weeks but if he has the surgery then it lessens the risk of maybe it happening again. All these things will be confirmed probably in the next 48 hours or so.

"Unfortunately, for us and Lawrence, it's a significant amount of time out and we just need to support him, as we do with all our injured players. He was starting to find his stride here and had obviously scored some important goals for us but that is football, unfortunately, the ups and downs of it.

"Best case scenario three months, probably worst-case scenario in terms of time would be about four months."

As well as league and League Cup fixtures, the striker will be unavailable for Scotland's Nations League matches from the end of September through mid-November.

New head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's side meet North Macedonia, Slovenia and Switzerland home and away this autumn. Shankland has scored seven goals in 22 international appearances, including three earlier this year.

After St Mirren, Rangers face Celtic at home in the League Cup then the same opponent away in the league before the first of this season's international breaks.

The Ibrox side have five games scheduled for October, three in November and six in December.

Meanwhile, winger Daisuke Yokota, who came on as a substitute against Motherwell, will also miss Rangers' match with St Mirren because of a groin injury but left-back Tuur Rommens is back in training and could return later this month.

No Shankland, no Chermiti - who will carry Rangers' goal threat?

After three goals in his previous two games - decisive contributions in wins at Aberdeen and Falkirk - prior to suffering his hamstring injury against Motherwell, Shankland's absence comes at a particularly bad time for him and for Rangers.

With fellow striker Youssef Chermiti expected to be out for a lengthy period after suffering anterior cruciate ligament damage against Hibernian last month, McInnes is now left without his two leading strikers.

"Having [Shankland] and Youssef out, two guys that guarantee you goals at Premiership level, there's no doubt it's a blow for us," McInnes said.

"Their disappointment's other people's opportunity as you've seen even from Saturday - Ryan getting his goal, Kevin [Kelsy] getting introduced, we've got Bojan Miovski, who knows his way about the Scottish Premiership, so it's not all doom and gloom on that front but it is disappointing news."

Rangers were good value for their win over Motherwell but with the number of chances they created it should have been more comfortable.

"If Lawrence Shankland was on the pitch throughout, he'd be walking away with a couple of goals," former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday said on BBC Sportsound.

Naderi capitalised on a blunder from Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen to roll the ball into an empty net. The big striker, who McInnes hinted would be called up by the Czech Republic, is a willing worker but can he deliver the sort of scoring numbers Shankland has consistently produced in the Premiership?

He scored three goals in his 11 games last season after joining Rangers in January, two of which came in the 8-0 Scottish Cup rout of lower-league Queen's Park. Naderi has three goals in eight appearances this term - one fewer than Shankland's four goals in 10 games.

Since joining Rangers, he has averaged a goal every 189 minutes. That figure is 146 minutes for Shankland, stretching back to the start of last season for Hearts.

The only striker on Rangers' books whose stats compare favourably with Shankland is North Macedonia international Miovski, who averages a goal every 148 minutes. However, the former Aberdeen favourite has found it difficult to get a consistent run in the side. Big-money signing Kelsy will come into the mix following his arrival from Portland Timbers.

The Venezuela forward had a golden opportunity to announce himself on his debut against Motherwell but showed little composure as his shot clipped the crossbar on its way out.

Of course, it is far too early to rush to judgement on Kelsy's ability to fill the Shankland void, but 13 goals in his past 46 games - averaging one every 190 minutes - would suggest the Ibrox club have not signed an out-and-out scorer.

"It's not an ideal scenario," former Rangers goalkeeper Cammy Bell said on the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast .

"They would have wanted to allow a little bit of time for Kelsy to find his feet in Scottish football and at Rangers. He's not going to get that now.

"You'd think Kelsy is going to be the one that will have to step up to the plate and score important goals because you can't rely on Shankland for now."

articles.title: Napoli’s Scott McTominay undergoes successful heart surgery
articles.summary: The midfielder, who will return to training in two weeks, will miss Wednesday’s Champions League game against Arsenal.
articles.body:
Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay has had successful surgery on a minor heart issue on Tuesday and will return to training in two weeks’ time, his club Napoli said.

The former Manchester United player recently experienced a heart rhythm disorder, something which is not considered serious but did require surgery.

“On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital. The operation was a complete success,” the Serie A club said in a statement.

“McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training.”

McTominay, 29, has been a key player for Napoli since joining from Manchester United in 2024, scoring 27 goals in 82 matches.

But he was off-form in their opening two Serie A games.

Napoli previously said McTominay would miss Scotland’s upcoming Nations League fixtures against Slovenia (twice), Switzerland and North Macedonia.

Napoli, who have just three points from their opening three Serie A games this season, host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday and then play Bologna and Fiorentina before the international break.

articles.standfirst: Alexia Putellas, Patri Guijarro, Mariona Caldentey, Mapi León, Claudia Pina y Cata Coll aspiran al preciado galardón
articles.summary: Alexia Putellas, Patri Guijarro, Mariona Caldentey, Mapi León, Claudia Pina y Cata Coll aspiran al preciado galardón
articles.body: Alexia Putellas, Patri Guijarro, Mariona Caldentey, Mapi León, Claudia Pina y Cata Coll forman parte de las 30 candidatas al Balón de Oro 2026, premio que se resolverá el próximo lunes 26 de octubre en el London Palladium de la capital inglesa. Además de la nominadas a 'Mejor Jugadora del Mundo', el fútbol femenino español tiene presencia en el resto de galardones al ser el Barcelona candidato a 'Mejor Club'; Pere Romeu y Jonatan Giráldez a 'Mejor Entrenador/a'; Cata Coll a 'Mejor Guardameta'; y Vicky López y Clara Serrajordi a 'Mejor Jugadora Joven'. Alexia Putellas (Barcelona), dos veces ganadora del Balón de Oro, lidera la lista de españolas que optan este año al premio. La que fuera capitana azulgrana, hoy del London City Lionneses amén de la selección española, disfruta de su quinta nominación a estos premios donde aparece como favorita en muchas quinielas [aunque el jurado aún no ha podido votar]. Su excelsa temporada, donde fue protagonista tanto de los éxitos de su equipo como de la selección, la vuelven a dar papeletas para conquistar un galardón que sólo su compañera Aitana Bonmatí -que no esta este año entre las nominadas- ha ganado en tres ocasiones. Además de la de Sant Pere de Ribas hay otras cinco españolas en la lista de candidatas a 'Mejor Jugadora del año': Patri Guijarro, cuyo nombre aparece por cuarta vez en estas listas; Mariona Caldentey, para quien es su tercera nominación y ya quedó segunda en la última edición; Mapi León, que aparece por segunda vez; Claudia Pina, que también repite nominación: y Cata Coll, que se estrena como candidata a este premio que nunca antes ha coronado a una guardameta. Además de las españolas están entre las nominadas tres jugadoras que militan en equipos españoles: Ewa Pajor (Barcerlona), Esmee Brugts (Barcelona) y Caroline Graham (Barcelona). El resto de aspirantes son Klara Bühl (Bayern de Múnich); Pernille Harder (Bayern); Momoko Tanikawa (Bayern); Wendie Renard (OL Lyonnes); Selma Bacha (OL Lyonnes); Caroline Weir (OL Lyonnes); Melchie Dumornay (OL Lyonnes); Alessia Russo (Arsenal); Khadikja Shaw (Manchester City); Alex Greenwood (Manchester City); Vivianne Miedema (Manchester City); Kerstin Casparik (Manchester City); Yui Hasegawa (Manchester City); Melvine Malard (Chelsea); Manaka Matsukubo (Chelsea); Tessa Wullaert (Como 1907); Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride); Rose Lavelle (Gotham); Temwa Chawinga (KC Current); Lorena (KC Current); Scarlett Camberos (Club América). El Barcelona competirá por ser nombrado como 'Mejor club femenino del año' ante el Bayern de Múnich, Manchester City, OL Lyonnes y Club América. Las azulgrana, que lograron el segundo póker de títulos de su historia (Liga, Copa de la Reina, Supercopa de España y Champions League), firmaron un bagaje sobresaliente: 45 partidos, 43 victorias, tres empates y una derrota con 188 goles a favor y sólo 20 en contra. Pere Romeu y Jonatan Giráldez son dos de los cinco candidatos a 'Mejor Entrenador/a del año', premio al que aspiran también Andrée Jeglertz, Nils Nielsen y Elena Sadiku. El técnico del Barcelona se impuso en la final de la Champions a su homólogo en el OL Lyonnes, con quien compartiera cuerpo técnico en el conjunto azulgrana. Cata Coll oposita a 'Mejor Guardameta del año' junto a Ann-Katrin Kerber, Hannah Hampton, Lorena y Ayaka Yamashita. La guardameta del Barcelona no sólo conquistó todos los títulos posibles con su club, sino que fue protagonista en la clasificación de España para el Mundial de Brasil de 2027 y ganaron la Nations League. Vicky López y Clara Serrajordi son dos de las cinco candidatas a 'Mejor Jugadora Joven del año', galardón al que también aspiran Felicia Schröder, Lily Yohannes y Veerle Buurman. Las dos jugadoras del Barcelona fueron grandes protagonistas el año paso tanto en el club como en la selección española.

articles.title: Antonio Cordón regresa a Olympiacos como director deportivo
articles.standfirst: El ex del Sevilla regresa a El Pireo para sustituir a Darko Kovacevic
articles.summary: El ex del Sevilla regresa a El Pireo para sustituir a Darko Kovacevic
articles.body: Antonio Cordón regresa... a Olympiacos. Aún no es oficial, pero el ex de Sevilla, Betis, Mónaco y Villarreal, entre otros, sustituirá a Darko Kovacevic, ex de la Real Sociedad, como director deportivo. Cabe recordar que el español, de 62 años, ya militó en el cuadro de El Pireo entre junio de 2023 y julio de 2024. Fue el 'arquitecto', de hecho, del equipo que terminó conquistando la Conference League -el único título continental en la historia del club- con José Luis Mendilibar en el banquillo en la 2023-24. Ya ese especuló con su regreso a Olympiacos a comienzos de verano, pero no cuajó. Sin embargo, la insistencia del cuadro que preside Evangelos Marinakis ha tenido 'premio'. Su objetivo volverá a ser el mismo que en su anterior etapa: liderar la reconstrucción deportiva -vienen de quedarse fuera de la Champions- y desarrollar un modelo multiclub junto a Nottingham Forest y Rio Ave. Cordón, que cuenta con un gran caché a nivel internacional, ha desechado numerosas ofertas, en especial de América Latina y Oriente Medio, desde que en junio abandonara el Sánchez Pizjuán. En Sevilla se vio limitado por el 'fair play' financiero, pero consiguió marcharse con la salvación en el bolsillo y habiendo liberado alrededor de 70 millones de euros. Era, hasta ahora, el último eslabón de más de dos décadas de experiencia en la dirección deportiva. Cordón fue, entre el año 200 y 2016, el 'arquitecto' del Villarreal que, con un modelo sostenible cimentado en la cantera, alcanzo la élite, se consolidó en Europa y alcanzó las semifinales de la Champions en la 2005-06. Fue, también, la 'cabeza visible', desde los despachos, del Mónaco que conquistó la Ligue 1 y alcanzó las semifinales de la Champions League en la 2016-17 con una joven hornada liderada por Mbappé, Bernardo Silva, Fabinho... Un equipo que terminó dejando 350 millones de euros en las arcas de El Principado. Como CEO de Hope Group (2017-20) logró varios hitos. Guió al Granada hasta Primera y a alcanzar los cuartos de la Europa League y devolvió al Parma a la Serie A con dos ascensos consecutivos. De vuelta a España, como director deportivo del Betis, sentó las bases para un ciclo de gran estabilidad deportiva que culminó con la Copa del Rey de 2022 y tres clasificaciones consecutivas para la Europa League.

articles.title: Celtic: Kasper Hogh & Kieran Tierney close to returns amid crucial spell
articles.summary: Manager Martin O'Neill confirms Celtic duo Kasper Hogh and Kieran Tierney could play a part in Wednesday's Scottish Premiership match at St Johnstone.
articles.body:
Manager Martin O'Neill has confirmed Celtic duo Kasper Hogh and Kieran Tierney could play a part in Wednesday's Scottish Premiership match at St Johnstone as the pair close in on returns from injury.

Denmark striker Hogh, who became the Scottish champions' record signing this summer, has not played since the second leg of Celtic's Champions League play-off defeat against LASK on 25 August.

Scotland defender Tierney missed the wins against Aberdeen and St Mirren.

"We've had Kasper back the last couple of days and Kieran did a little bit of work with us [on Tuesday] morning, so we'll have a look to see how they are," O'Neill said.

"We've got a couple of other fitness issues for players but we'll try and go as strong as we possibly can."

On whether he is hopeful Hogh and Tierney could play some part on Wednesday, O'Neill added: "Yeah, obviously Kasper's had the extra day, we'll see how they are [on Wednesday]."

How much will Celtic miss Asian Games-bound Yang?

Visit our Celtic page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Get Celtic news notifications in the BBC Sport app

'Exceptional' Yang a 'big miss' for Celtic

In the absence of Hogh, who has scored three times in five Celtic appearances since joining from Bodo/Glimt, fellow big-money summer arrival Camilo Duran has excelled playing at centre-forward.

The Colombian has netted six goals in eight matches this term but, when asked about whether Hogh's return would mean Duran moving back out to a wide area, O'Neill said "it's a matter of trying to get your best players on the field".

The Celtic boss will be without winger Yang Hyun-jun for the encounter with St Johnstone as the South Korea international takes part in the Asian Games.

O'Neill says the 24-year-old, who will be absent for his club's next four matches, will be a "big miss", with two derby meetings against Rangers to come either side of a Europa League opener with Ferencvaros following Wednesday's action.

"He's playing exceptionally well for what he does with the ball," the veteran manager said of Yang. "It's terrific, he's scored a couple of very important goals for us.

"And what he's doing without the ball, I don't think anybody could question his work rate for us at the football club. He's been great but he's been great since I've come in here."

Celtic are on the road again on Sunday when they make the short trip to Govan to face their city rivals at Ibrox (12:00 BST).

However, O'Neill would not allow himself to be distracted by his side's Premier Sports Cup quarter-final and insists Wednesday's game holds more significance.

The 74-year-old added: "I genuinely can't [have one eye on it] and that's honestly where I think, first of all, we have to play our game.

"We have to try and defend a title. We have to try and win a football match.

"And to me, this game is far more important than Sunday's match."

articles.title: FIFA accused of ‘abusive conduct’ over women’s football calendar in Europe
articles.summary: European Leagues body first filed complaint to the European Commission to protect men’s players in October 2024.
articles.body:
A legal complaint against FIFA has been extended to cover its alleged “abusive conduct” towards the women’s game in Europe.

The complaint by the European Leagues umbrella group, which includes the Premier League and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) as members, was first lodged with the European Commission on behalf of men’s players in October 2024.

The complaint claims that FIFA abused a dominant position under European competition law in allegedly failing to properly consult with leagues over the men’s international match calendar announced in 2023.

European Leagues formally welcomed 14 European women’s leagues to its ranks in June, including the Women’s Super League in England and the Scottish Women’s Premier League, and has now extended the legal complaint to cover the impact on the women’s international match calendar.

A European Leagues statement on Tuesday said: “European Leagues is extending the scope of its complaint to the European Commission about the international match calendar to include FIFA’s abusive conduct regarding the women’s international match calendar and related women’s football regulatory decisions.

“FIFA’s conduct threatens the growth and financial sustainability of women’s professional leagues, and risks player health and wellbeing.

“The European Commission must now act to ensure that EU law is respected and that the future of women’s professional football is not determined unilaterally by FIFA,” the European Leagues said.

“The submission details the same pattern of conduct identified in the original complaint: FIFA holds conflicting roles as governing body and competition organizer, which gives rise to a conflict of interest,” they added.

“As in men’s football, FIFA consistently uses its regulatory power to favour its own competition and commercial interests to the detriment of women’s football and of European national leagues.”

FIFA has been approached for comment, and has previously insisted that the calendar announced at its 2023 Congress was the result of extensive consultation with all stakeholders, including leagues.

It has also said it is fully within its rights to set the parameters of its own competitions like the Club World Cup provided they fit within the agreed calendar framework.

The ratcheting up of the legal pressure on FIFA comes at a time when its President, Gianni Infantino, remains under fire from three continental confederations over his controversial plan to seek private investment in a company to run the men’s and women’s World Cups and other FIFA competitions.

The plan, since abandoned, foresaw a company called FIFA Forward Enterprise being set up, which would be 20 percent owned by private investors.

European Leagues’ statement on Tuesday said the controversy over the company “further exposed this structural conflict (between FIFA’s position as a regulator and commercial operator) and vividly illustrates how profit-driven motives taint FIFA’s regulatory decisions and decision-making processes”.

articles.title: Lionel Messi, Rose Lavelle Headline 2026 Men's, Women's Ballon d'Or Nominees
articles.summary: The nominees for the 2026 men's and women's Ballon d'Or were officially announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
The nominees for the 2026 men's and women's Ballon d'Or were officially announced Tuesday.

Multiple past Ballon d'Or winners were included on the men's list, including reigning winner Ousmane Dembélé of Paris Saint-Germain, 2024 winner Rodri of Barcelona and eight-time winner Lionel Messi of Inter Miami:

For the women, 2021 and 2022 winner Alèxia Putellas of London City Lionesses made the list, as did the past two runners-up in Caroline Graham Hansen of Barcelona and Mariona Caldentey of Arsenal:

The battle for both awards appears to be wide open with no single player standing out as a clear and obvious favorite.

On the men's side, Bayern Munich's Harry Kane is listed as a slight favorite ahead of Barcelona's Lamine Yamal on OddsChecker.com , followed by Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé and then Rodri.

Other big names such as Messi, Dembélé, Manchester City's Erling Haaland and Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham are further down the list despite strong showings at the FIFA World Cup for Argentina, France, England and Norway, respectively.

Kane scored a remarkable 61 goals in 51 matches across all competitions for Bayern last season, plus he scored six goals for an England squad that reached the 2026 FIFA World Cup semifinals and finished in third place.

Should Kane prevail, it will mark his first Ballon d'Or, and the first by an Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001.

Both Yamal and Rodri had impressive World Cups in their own right, leading Spain to their second-ever World Cup triumph.

Messi, 39, already holds the record for most Ballon d'Or wins with eight, and he proved once again in the United States that he remains among the best players in the world, scoring eight goals, as Argentina reached the World Cup final.

The women's Ballon d'Or is more unpredictable than it has been in years since reigning three-time winner Aitana Bonmatí of Barcelona was not named a nominee after missing much of last season with a leg injury.

Putellas may be the woman to beat for the 2026 award, as the two-time women's Ballon d'Or winner scored 20 goals across all competitions last season and led Barca to Liga F and UEFA Women's Champions League titles in 2025-26.

Her win is far from guaranteed, though, as Arsenal's Alessia Russo led the squad to the FIFA Women's Champion Cup title, while scoring 24 goals across all competitions.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw is also firmly in the mix by virtue of her 27 goals and City winning the Women's Super League.

The lone American representative among the women's Ballon d'Or nominees is Rose Lavelle, who led Gotham FC to the 2025 NWSL championship and 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup title.

The winners of the 2026 men's and women's Ballon d'Or Awards will be announced on Oct. 26 in London.

articles.title: El mejor Alavés de la historia
articles.standfirst: Quique Sánchez Flores, que cogió al equipo en marzo peleando por salvarse, ha transformado a los babazorros en un conjunto de autor
articles.summary: Quique Sánchez Flores, que cogió al equipo en marzo peleando por salvarse, ha transformado a los babazorros en un conjunto de autor
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores ha instalado el estado de felicidad en Vitoria. El técnico madrileño cogió a un equipo en caída libre el pasado mes de marzo, logró certificar la permanencia más cara de los últimos tiempos y esta temporada quiere saltar de pantalla. Sólo son cuatro jornadas, pero, de momento, el inicio de curso del Alavés es el mejor de su historia: tres triunfos y un empate para situarse en la segunda posición de la tabla. La dinámica que atraviesa el Glorioso es una continuación de los números del equipo desde que aterrizó Sánchez Flores en el banquillo de Mendizorroza el pasado 3 de marzo. Desde entonces, se han disputado 16 jornadas y sólo Barcelona y Real Madrid han sumado más puntos que el Alavés. 26 de 48 posibles para un equipo que ha marcado goles en todos estos partidos y con una trayectoria de Champions desde su desembarco. El Alavés de Quique es un equipo vertical y dinámico, que avasalla al rival a golpe de centro lateral, poderoso en los duelos, al que los rivales ya no le corren tanto a los espacios, que necesita muy poco para marcar y que también ha evidenciado una mejoría defensiva, su asignatura pendiente el año pasado. Los jugadores creen en el mensaje de su técnico y el fútbol de este Alavés casa mucho mejor con lo que ha sido el equipo a lo largo de su historia. El trabajo de Coudet fue notable, pero en Mendizorroza siempre hubo cierto escepticismo con el libreto del técnico argentino. Quique ha caído de pie en Vitoria, se ganó al vestuario en un momento delicado a base de transmitir tranquilidad y los hechos, en forma de victorias, no han hecho más que refrendar la apuesta a largo plazo que hizo Josean Querejeta por el técnico madrileño en el mes de marzo. La experiencia del técnico fue clave la pasada campaña para gestionar una situación complicada y su mano izquierda le ha permitido explotar la capacidad goleadora de Boyé y Toni Martínez, agilizar el crecimiento de jugadores como Ángel Pérez o Pablo Ibáñez, mantener el liderazgo de tipos como Antonio Blanco o Tenaglia y hasta domar a un Mariano en el que sólo él ha creído. El primer proyecto desde cero de Quique coincide con el verano en el que menos movimientos ha sufrido la plantilla. Y esa es la gran noticia. Por Vitoria han llegado ofertas por jugadores como Blanco, Toni Martínez, Boyé o Sivera. Sin embargo, el Alavés, un club históricamente vendedor, ha priorizado esta temporada mantener a todos sus referentes. Eso permitió a Quique echar a trabajar en el mes de julio con gran parte del bloque hecho y afrontar el inicio de curso en las mejores condiciones, algo cada vez más complicado para muchos clubes. El técnico ya avisó en el Carlos Tartiere tras certificar la permanencia que el desafío para esta temporada era salir de la parte baja. Esquivar sufrimientos y abrazar la tranquilidad. De momento, va por buen camino. Sólo han transcurrido cuatro jornadas y la posición del Alavés no deja de ser anecdótica, pero los 10 puntos que suma no se los va a quitar nadie

articles.title: Man Utd have highest transfer net spend since 2022 but Champions League return will test depth - Between the Lines
articles.summary: Manchester United have spent over £1bn on signings since 2022 but do they have the squad to handle the extra workload of Champions League football? Between the Lines breaks down the challenge ahead for Michael Carrick after a poor start to the campaign
articles.body:
But, after a disappointing start to the new campaign, how will they handle the challenge of juggling three games per week? And has their rebuild neglected one key part of their squad?

With no European football and early exits from the Carabao Cup and FA Cup against Grimsby Town and Brighton respectively, Manchester United only played 40 games in all competitions last term.

It was the joint-fewest of any Premier League side and the club's lowest total for a single season since the 1913/14 campaign.

The light schedule allowed Carrick to keep key players fresh while Manchester United's rivals were having to rotate. In the period between his appointment and the conclusion of the Premier League season, only five sides made fewer line-up changes than United.

That level of consistency in terms of selection is unlikely to be possible this season, with Thursday's game against Sabah the first of eight guaranteed Champions League fixtures. Manchester United could play as many as 67 games across all competitions.

Carrick has talked up the positives of a more demanding schedule.

"It's less training once the season gets going, but a lot more involvement for the players," he said during pre-season. Carrick also made the point that the majority of his players are more accustomed to playing in Europe than not.

But the return to continental competition is still a test of their squad. The last time Manchester United juggled European commitments, in 2024/25, they finished 15th.

They should be well-equipped to cope with the extra workload.

Manchester United spent a middling £163m on new signings during the summer transfer window but they have invested more than £1bn in total since 2022 and have the highest net spend of any Premier League club in that timeframe, at £769.5m.

But there has been a lack of balance in their spending.

This summer, it was focused almost entirely on their midfield, with Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans the headline additions. A year ago, most of the money went on their attack as they signed Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

Their defence has so far been neglected.

Only 19 per cent of the £1bn spent since 2022 has gone on defenders. It is the third-lowest percentage of Premier League clubs in the same period, above only Liverpool and Everton, and falls way short of the 42 per cent spent on their forwards.

The result is the squad, although stronger in some areas, still lacks quality and depth in others. Manchester United's forwards are rated as the third-most valuable of the Premier League's big six but their midfielders and defenders are the least valuable.

And there are still question marks even in attack, where they have an abundance of supporting forwards including Mbeumo, Cunha and Amad Diallo, but only one out-and-out striker in Sesko.

They also lack a playmaking alternative to Bruno Fernandes.

Despite spending upwards of £1bn over the last four years, Manchester United's team shows little turnover.

Amazingly, their back four for Sunday's 2-2 draw against Everton, made up of Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot, was the same as in Erik Ten Hag's first game in May 2022.

Marcus Rashford's return to the fold, to the left of Fernandes, means six starters were the same in total, adding to the sense of a side that has gone stale, despite the club's huge spending.

Their retention rate of 54.5 per cent, from the first game of the 2022/23 season to the latest game of the new campaign, is by far the highest of any club, with Arsenal next on 36.4 per cent having retained Gabriel, Ben White, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka.

Continuity can of course be positive. But while Gabriel, White, Odegaard and Saka have all played crucial roles in turning Arsenal into Premier League champions, many of Manchester United's retained starters are better known for underperformance.

The issue for Carrick, as he prepares to manage a far busier Manchester United schedule, is that his other options, particularly in defence, do not inspire much confidence either.

It all adds up to make his task tougher than last season.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 nominees: Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice nominated
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is one of three England players nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or alongside Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is one of three England players nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham and Arsenal's Declan Rice join Kane, the favourite for the award, on the 30-player shortlist.

Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi, who is looking to win his ninth Ballon d'Or, has been nominated.

The 39-year-old scored eight goals as Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain in July, with Messi since retiring from international football.

Lamine Yamal is one of six Spain players that won the World Cup to be included.

Having scored the winning goal in the final, Paris St-Germain forward Ferran Torres, who joined the French club from Barcelona in the summer, makes the cut.

Back-to-back Champions League winners Paris St-Germain have nine players - excluding new signing Torres - nominated, including last year's winner Ousmane Dembele.

Real Madrid forwards Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr also make the shortlist, as do Arsenal defenders Gabriel and William Saliba.

The award is celebrating its 70th anniversary, having been created by France Football in 1956, and the winner will be announced at an ceremony in London on 26 October.

The "symbolic choice of venue" is in tribute to former England player Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the first Ballon d'Or.

articles.title: El Real Madrid deja de 'silenciar' el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El año pasado, tras lo sucedido con Vinicius en 2024, no se hicieron eco de las nominaciones ni de los resultados del galardón
articles.summary: El año pasado, tras lo sucedido con Vinicius en 2024, no se hicieron eco de las nominaciones ni de los resultados del galardón
articles.body: El Real Madrid está de vuelta en el Balón de Oro. No es que se hubiera ido. Es que el año pasado, tras conocerse los 30 nominados que optaban al premio que acabó llevándose Dembélé, el club blanco no se hizo eco en sus canales oficiales de ninguno de los nominados... ni de los resultados finales. La razón fue lo sucedido en 2024, cuando Rodri Hernández se hizo con el galardón por delante de Vinicius con el posterior plante de la expedición blanca, que se quedó en tierra tras conocer que el extremo brasileño no sería finalmente el ganador tras haber levantado Liga y Champions en la 2023-24. Aquella decepción y enfado monumental para el club, que consideró una injusticia lo sucedido, el club blanco lo dejó claro desde ese mismo 28 de octubre de 2024: "Ahora mismo, el Balón de Oro deja de existir". De hecho, la entidad llegó a cancelar la programación especial de casi cinco horas que tenían con motivo del Balón de Oro en RMTV. Sin embargo, el club blanco sí que se ha hecho eco este año a través de sus redes sociales y con una noticia en su propia web oficial. "Mbappé, Vini Jr., Bellingham y Cucurella integran la lista de 30 candidatos al Balón de Oro 2026, que entrega la revista France Football. Los nominados han sido elegidos por sus méritos durante la temporada 2025/26", explican.

articles.title: Isra Suero brilla con el Castellón mientras medita su futuro
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista lidera a los albinegros en la victoria frente al Albacete en medio de rumores sobre su salida al Maccabi
articles.summary: El centrocampista lidera a los albinegros en la victoria frente al Albacete en medio de rumores sobre su salida al Maccabi
articles.body: El centrocampista Israel Suero ha sido protagonista destacado en la victoria del Castellón frente al Albacete por 2-0 después de marcar el segundo del conjunto de la Plana y llevar en volandas al equipo en los 33 minutos que estuvo en el terreno de juego. El futbolista madrileño brilló en el campo mientras tiene sobre la mesa una oferta del Maccabi de Tel Aviv para su inmediata incorporación. El jugador trasladó la propuesta al club orellut en vísperas del partido de la jornada 3 frente al Celta Fortuna, tal como reconoció su técnico Pablo Hernández. Suero no jugó ese partido. Tampoco concretó su salida a la conclusión del mercado. No obstante, su marcha aún puede producirse, toda vez que en algunas ligas sigue abierta la opción de fichar. Es el caso de Israel, país donde podría recalar y cuya ventana estival se cierra el 16 de septiembre. Tras la brillante actuación de Suero frente al Albacete su técnico, Pablo Hernández, reconoció su deseo de que permanezca en la disciplina albinegra, aunque no garantizó su continuidad. "Le he dicho que estoy encantado con él y me gustaría que se quedara. Es un jugador determinante para nosotros y lo que tenía que hablar con él ya se lo dije. Él sabe que será importante si se queda", ha comentado. El rol de Suero como albinegro en el último año y medio ha sido el de revulsivo en las segundas partes, función en la que ha destacado en muchos partidos, como el del pasado domingo, en el que marcó cinco minutos después de ingresar en el terreno de juego. Ahora le corresponde al jugador decidir si permanece en el Castellón o acepta la oferta del Maccabi, en cuyo caso también tendría que haber un acuerdo entre clubes. El madrileño, de 32 años, finaliza contrato con la entidad de la Plana al final de esta temporada.
