articles.title: Jerry Sandusky Appears Remotely in Court as Lawyers Prepare a Federal Court Bid to Seek a New Trial
articles.summary: BELLEFONTE, Pa. (AP) — Former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky appeared in court remotely Tuesday where he said he agreed with his lawyers not to go forward with testimony from an accuser who wants to recant allegations that Sandusky sexually abused him years ago.
articles.body:
BELLEFONTE, Pa. (AP) — Former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky appeared in court remotely Tuesday where he said he agreed with his lawyers not to go forward with testimony from an accuser who wants to recant allegations that Sandusky sexually abused him years ago.

The hearing was part of the latest bid by Sandusky's lawyers to secure a new trial for him as his lawyers prepare to go to federal court to seek a new trial after failing repeatedly in state courts.

In court, Sandusky, 82, appeared on a video screen in a spare room in Laurel Highlands state prison, seated at a small table in a maroon-colored shirt looking up at the camera through glasses. Under questioning, he told Centre County Judge Maureen Skerda he had consulted with his lawyers about the decision not to present the accuser's testimony recanting the allegations from Sandusky's 2012 trial.

"I'm making this decision on advice of counsel," Sandusky said, his arms on the table in front of him, a notepad between them. "Is there anything wrong with that?"

Sandusky, 82, has been serving a decades-long prison sentence since he was convicted of 45 counts of sexual abuse in 2012, after eight young men testified about what happened to them as boys.

Sandusky's lawyer, Jerry Russo, told reporters later that courts frown on granting new trials based on a witness recantation, seeing it as "inherently unreliable." Instead, Russo said he plans to take Sandusky's broader claims for a new trial to federal court — Sandusky's made at least three attempts in state courts — after one more procedural appeal in state court.

Judge Skerda told Russo and Sandusky that withdrawing the request to present the recantation from the accuser, identified in court documents as R.R., meant that it could not be litigated again in state or federal court.

The Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General had said the supposed recantation was "highly suspect." Sandusky's lawyers have said in court filings that R.R.'s allegations were "based on suggestive leading questioning, prosecutorial coercion and influence, confirmatory bias and memory manipulation."

Sandusky was the defensive coordinator at one of the country's top football programs under Hall of Fame head coach Joe Paterno. The scandal led to Paterno's firing, and the university paid more than $100 million to people who said they were abused by Sandusky.

Authorities said he found and groomed boys at The Second Mile, a charity he founded for at-risk youth. Sandusky has repeatedly declared his innocence .

R.R., who was 25 years old at trial, testified that when he was 11, Sandusky sexually abused him in the coach's basement in 1998, a transcript shows.

articles.title: Every Way You Can Play Pokémon
articles.body:
Pokémon is more than just a game. It’s an entire community of fans both young and old who want to catch ‘em all. What you may not know is that however you engage with Pokémon, chances are there’s a way to take your fandom to the next level by participating in all sorts of Pokémon organised play events.

Whether a lifelong veteran or a brand new fan, here are the best ways to play Pokémon and participate in an ever-growing community. It all starts with finding your local Play! Pokémon store . They’re the perfect place to learn how to play, meet like-minded people, and level up your skills. It’s all about having fun!

It can be intimidating to get into a trading card game that’s been going since 1996, but Pokémon makes it easy to immerse yourself in all things TCG and begin participating in events.

A great place to start is at a Prerelease event. Prereleases provide a great opportunity to learn the rules of the game, build a deck, and play in a friendly, casual environment. As a bonus, you get to go home with cards from a brand new expansion before anyone else!

League Nights are where you can bring along your deck to test it against other players. These weekly gatherings offer a relaxed environment where you can trade cards, and play against fellow Pokémon fans. This is where you can really learn the ins and outs of the game in a welcoming environment.

Once you’ve become familiar with the rules of the Pokémon TCG, there are monthly events that really put your skills to the test. These tournaments are known as League Challenges, where you can earn prizes and get to spend quality time with other players. There are also League Cups, high-level local tournaments which are perfect for forging your path to becoming a true Pokémon master.

Celebrating 10 years in 2026, Pokémon GO turns your everyday world into a Pokémon-filled wonderland. It’s the closest you can get to becoming a real-life Pokémon trainer, filling your Pokédex on your quest to become the ultimate Pokémon master. Through your screen, Pokémon appear in your surroundings, and you can catch, train, and battle them. Anyone can pick up and play Pokémon GO. All you have to do is download the game for free on any mobile device. GO features monthly global community days, which encourage players to play together and feature more frequent Pokémon spawns. Plus, there are increased chances to encounter and catch highly-coveted shiny Pokémon.

Pokémon League events aren’t exclusive to the TCG either. Your local Play! Store will have Pokémon GO League Challenges, which provide entry-level events to test your skills, and even Pokémon GO League Cup Tournaments, where you can really dig in and strive to be the very best.

One of the newest ways to play is Pokémon Champions, which launched in April 2026. It’s a free-to-play game available on the Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2, as well as iOS and Android devices. It’s a game all about good old fashioned Pokémon battles; you assemble your favorite Pokémon (via Pokemon HOME or by recruiting them in-game), and battle opponents from all around the world in 2-on-2 battles.

There are events at your local Play! Store where you can play Champions. All you need to do is bring your Nintendo Switch to your store’s Video Game Challenge. These are entry-level tournaments that provide a fun atmosphere, and also an opportunity to play alongside fellow gamers to ease yourself into competitive play. From there, you can participate in in-person Video Game Cups – higher-level tournaments where you can play among friends and bring out your very best Pokémon to win prizes.

Whether you prefer the TCG, Pokémon GO, or Pokemon Champions, the opportunities to be involved in the Pokémon organised play community are limitless. So find your local Play! Store and explore fresh ways to be a part of Pokémon today.

articles.title: Lawrence Shankland: Rangers captain expected to be out for three to four months with hamstring tear, confirms Derek McInnes
articles.summary: Striker Lawrence Shankland was forced off during Rangers' win against Motherwell on Saturday; he has suffered a hamstring issue similar to the one that kept him out for three months at Hearts last season; the 31-year-old has scored four goals in 10 appearances for the Ibrox club
articles.body:
Derek McInnes confirmed his 31-year-old skipper has suffered a recurrence of the injury when both were at Hearts last season, which ruled him out for nine weeks.

Shankland, who has scored four goals in 10 Rangers appearances so far this season, was forced off early in Saturday's 1-0 home league win over Motherwell. His replacement Ryan Naderi scored the game's only goal.

Ahead of the Premiership clash with St Mirren at Ibrox on Wednesday night, McInnes said: "He's had his scan with confirmation that he's had a tear.

"It's a 2C tear and similar to the one he did previously at Hearts in January.

"And he's actually in London now, he's getting an ultrasound scan, a follow-up scan, which is just to determine whether, with the specialist, he has surgery or whether he'll just let it heal naturally like he did the last time.

"We will probably have a better idea on the aftermath of that scan and discussion with specialists just how long the injury is going to be.

"My little knowledge I have of it is that if he has the surgery then he might be an extra three or four weeks.

"But if he has a surgery, then it lessens a risk of it maybe happening again, but, again, all these things will be confirmed probably in the next 48 hours or so, but unfortunately for us and Lawrence, it's a significant amount of time out.

"I think best-case scenario, three months, probably worst-case scenario in terms of time about four months. But I think the specialist appointment in London will maybe shed a bit of light on that and get a bit more clarity."

Naderi came on to score the only goal against the Steelmen and Rangers did bring in £9m striker Kevin Kelsy on Deadline Day, so you could argue it is not an area they are short in.

But Shankland's injury comes after they had already lost forward Youssef Chermiti for a "significant period" with an ACL injury.

There is also Bojan Miovski, but he has struggled to get a consistent run since his move to Ibrox from Girona last summer.

He scored 13 in all competitions in his first season at Ibrox, averaging a goal every 142 minutes. Naderi's average for Rangers last season was a goal every 203 minutes.

Compare that to Shankland's average under McInnes at Hearts last season - that was a goal every 86.5 minutes.

McInnes added: "We just need to support him as we do with all our injured players, but having him and Youssef out, guys who guarantee you goals at Premiership level, there's no doubt it's a blow for us.

"But their disappointments are other people's opportunities as you've seen, even from Saturday, Ryan getting his goal and Kevin [Kelsy] getting introduced.

"We have Bojan Miovski, who knows his way about the Premiership as well, so it's not all doom and gloom on that front, but it is disappointing news."

articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Declan Rice, Jude Bellingham among nominees but no Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.summary: The 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees have been announced; 2026 marks the 70th edition, with the ceremony being held outside of Paris for the very first time in celebration; the 2026 ceremony takes place in London, England on October 26
articles.body:
Harry Kane is among those in the running for the men's prize and is the bookmakers' favourite to be crowned.

Kane scored 73 goals last season, enjoying one of the best campaigns of his career and he could become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane is joined the 30-man long-list by international teammates Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.

Other Premier League stars like Bruno Fernandes, Erling Haaland, Gabriel and William Saliba are among the other players included.

Lamine Yamal, Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe will be the likely challengers to Kane for the illustrious award but there is no nomination for Cristiano Ronaldo despite winning the Saudi Pro League with Al-Nassr.

England stars Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood are among 30 players nominated for the women's Ballon d'Or.

Kerim Alajbegovic (RB Salzburg/Juventus)

Ayyoub Bouaddi - (Lille/Manchester City)

Women's Young Talent of the Year nominees

The 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony will take place on October 26, 2026 in London.

How are the Ballon d'Or winners decided?

The shortlist was compiled by a group of journalists from France Football working alongside French sports publication L'Equipe.

For the men's Ballon d'Or prize, winners are decided by a voting system involving one journalist from each of the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations.

Each journalist casts votes for their top 10 players from the 30-player shortlist. The 10 players are awarded 15, 12, 10, seven, five, four, three, two and one point based on where they rank.

If players are tied on points, then whoever has the most first-place rankings from the 100 journalists finishes ahead on points. If that is tied, then it's the most second-places and so on.

Journalists are encouraged to consider three factors when deciding their vote:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character

For the women's Ballon d'Or, the same process applies but only journalists from the top-50 ranked nations are invited to vote.

articles.title: El campeón tiene un genio
articles.standfirst: Un doblete de Yáñez encarrila el triunfo del Madrid en su estreno en la Youth, al que pondría la guinda un gol de Santamaría
articles.summary: Un doblete de Yáñez encarrila el triunfo del Madrid en su estreno en la Youth, al que pondría la guinda un gol de Santamaría
articles.body: Comenzó a lo grande el camino de la defensa del título que tan brillantemente consiguiera el Real Madrid juvenil dirigido por Álvaro López. El técnico aumentó las vitrinas blancas con la consecución de la tan perseguida segunda Youth League y afronta esta nueva campaña con el objetivo de reeditar título continental. Para ello la plantilla de este año presenta nuevas incorporaciones, pero con refuerzos importantes. Una mezcla de talento con la que el Madrid presentó su candidatura a una nueva Youth con un triunfo incontestable ante el Inter. Porque entre otras cosas, el campeón tiene un genio: Yáñez. El extremo firmó un espectacular doblete para encarrilar un triunfo que Fran Santamaría cerró con un gol en el último minuto del partido. El Inter de Milán ha sido la primera 'víctima' de este súper Real Madrid juvenil. Eléctrico y veloz en las asociaciones y con presión muy alta y efectiva en la recuperación del balón, los blancos hicieron que la primera parte fuera una pesadilla para los italianos. El debut en esta competición de Yeremaiah, o la imponente presencia de Cherif en la medular, vuelve a poner de manifiesto que las joyas en la Fábrica siguen puliéndose. El gol tardó en llegar media hora por el buen trabajo defensivo interista. Un 'muro' que derribó una genialidad. Yáñez amagó con habilidad en el área y 'fusiló' aprovechando un error defensivo a la hora de despejar el buen balón largo que Joan puso a la espalda de la zaga italiana. Lacosta pudo marcar el segundo poco después, en una recuperación tras presión, aunque su disparo se marchó cerca de la base del poste. El conjunto interista movió el banco para buscar la igualada desde el arranque de la segunda mitad y aunque sus prestaciones mejoraron, la puerta de Guille Ponce se mantuvo tranquila. El potencial y la calidad de los hombres de Álvaro López afloraron y el resultado fue el segundo tanto de Dani Yáñez. Un golazo marca de la casa en el que el gaditano, en una carrera poderosa ganando el interior, supera con un duro zurdazo a Farronato desde la frontal. Mérito al arranque de la jugada para un gran Lezcano, quien de manera limpia robó el esférico para encontrar la conexión letal con el bigoleador. Fran Santamaría marcó el tercero y definitivo con la asistencia de Company pocos segundos antes del pitido final. El delantero, fichado del Castellón, protagoniza la semana de su debut oficial con tres goles, tras el doblete en el partido liguero. Muy buenas sensaciones en todas las líneas en esta primera victoria del conjunto blanco que tras la contundente victoria del fin de semana, volverá a optar al ‘triplete’ que consiguió la pasada campaña. Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): Ponce; Guille (66’ Espi), Joan Martínez, Mateo Garrido, Lezcano; Lacosta, Cherif (55’ Corcoba), Carlos Díez © (82’ Company); Yáñez, Yeremiah (66’ Santamaría) y Ciria (81’ Sergio Castellón). Entrenador: Álvaro López. Inter de Milán (4-4-2): Farronato; Moranduzzo, Donato, Mackewicz, Sorino (46’ Dario Rocca); D’Agostino, La Torre © (80’ Kartelo), G. Fasana (63’ Ali Maghlout); Franchi (46’ Virtuani), Carrara (73’ Matarrese), El Mahboubi. Entrenador: Emiliano Bigica. Goles: 1-0 (32’) Yáñez; 2-0 (62’) Yáñez; 3-0 (93’) Fran Santamaría. Árbitro: Giorgi Avazashvili (Georgia). Amonestó con cartulina amarilla a La Torre (31’), Carrara (48’), Cherif (51’), Mateo Garrido (64’) y Lezcano (73’). articles.title: Celtic: Martin O'Neill could rejig system to accommodate his best players against St Johnstone, live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Record signing Kasper Hogh is available after injury; Hyun Jun Yang is on international duty with South Korea; Watch St Johnstone vs Celtic on Wednesday night, live on Sky Sports from 7.30pm
articles.body:
Camilo Duran has shone in the centre-forward role in Hogh's three-game absence with a groin problem.

The Colombian netted three times and set up the winner for Yang in Saturday's 2-1 victory over St Mirren, as well as having a goal controversially disallowed for offside.

Duran previously impressed out wide, but arrived at Celtic from Qarabag as a striker.

O'Neill has another current option up front in on-loan Chelsea forward Shim Mheuka, who also had a goal disallowed in Paisley and looked a threat during two substitute appearances.

Callum Osmand is also due back from an ankle injury next month and with South Korea winger Yang missing four matches for the Asian Games, O'Neill could be tempted to experiment with the 3-5-2 formation he favoured during his first spell as Hoops manager.

"We've got Kasper back the last couple of days and Kieran (Tierney) did a little bit of work with us, so we'll have a look to see how they are. We've got a couple of other fitness issues with players, but will try to go as strongly as we possibly can," the 74-year-old said ahead of Wednesday's game at St Johnstone, live on Sky Sports.

"Whatever we do, when everybody is absolutely fit, then it's a matter of trying to get your best players on the field." Mheuka, 18, looks set to stake a claim.

"I expect decent things of Shim," O'Neill said. "I expect him to do well.

"He's just getting to know the players. He's getting to know what's expected of him in terms of style of play, what we do with the ball and what we do without it.

"It's essentially what he does with the ball that will determine not only his time here, but his future in the game and he looks a player.

"We definitely have got better options up front than we had last season."

England youth international Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow determined to make an impact.

"I'm just focused on playing and training, trying to get into that team and come on and make an impact whenever I can," he said.

"When you come on, in your mind, you want to try and take that one opportunity that might come to you.

"It's just about staying positive whenever you can, always believe in putting yourself in the right positions and, ultimately, I'll get chances.

"You can't get anywhere without self-belief. We're all in positions where you want to be because of how confident we are in our abilities and how much we believe in ourselves."

Simo Valakari's Saints have won their opening two home Premiership games.

"It's nice to see really talented young managers doing well," O'Neill said.

"They want to play football and they're committed. There's a vitality about them which is very, very encouraging. Not dissimilar in many aspects to what Craig McLeish is doing at St Mirren."

articles.title: PSG's Champions League treble bid is hardest test yet - Marquinhos
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos admits his side face their biggest challenge yet as they bid for a "historic" third straight Champions League triumph....
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos admits his side face their biggest challenge yet as they bid for a "historic" third straight Champions League triumph.

Holders PSG launch their European campaign against Slovan Bratislava at Parc des Princes on Wednesday night having defended their crown last season.

Only three other clubs have previously been crowned European champions for three consecutive seasons - Real Madrid (twice - 1956-60 and 2016-18), Ajax (1971-73) and Bayern Munich (1974-76).

Marquinhos told a press conference: "It would be historic. It is difficult to win it once. Winning it twice is even harder and very few teams have won it three times in a row, so that shows how difficult it is and I can appreciate the effort involved.

"It is about ambition, motivation and philosophy. We know that everything we have won is in the past now, so if we win it again we will have to be very demanding with ourselves and keep our standards high.

"Other teams have made important signings and efforts to improve their squads. I think it will be even harder this season than in previous ones."

Luis Enrique, nominated on Friday for the 2026 Ballon d'Or coach of the year award, described his side's start to the season as "catastrophic" after a four-match winless run in all competitions.

Following PSG's European Super Cup win over Aston Villa last month, they lost to French Cup winners Lens in the Trophee des Champions and drew their first two Ligue 1 games against Rennes and Lille before losing their opening home game to Monaco last week.

Luis Enrique, whose side sit 14th in Ligue 1, told a press conference: "If we are just talking about results, it has been a catastrophic start to the season.

"We try to assess everything that happens on the pitch. Of course, there are things to improve. I think we deserve more points, but I accept it and we are working hard to improve our performance."

Slovan coach Yaya Toure has guided the Slovakian champions to the Champions League proper for the second time in their history after being appointed as head coach in July.

The former Barcelona and Manchester City midfielder's side have knocked out Iberia Tbilisi, Mjallby and Celje after entering the competition in the second qualifying round.

Luis Enrique added: "I always try to transmit the same thing to my players: the past is the past. You have to renew yourselves every year.

"Everyone is motivated and excited at the idea of playing us. It's something we have to accept and that's why we have to look to get out of our comfort zone. We have to seek to reinvent ourselves every day."

articles.title: Andrea Belotti ficha... ¡por el Modena de Serie B!
articles.summary: 'Il Gallo' estaba sin equipo
articles.body: Un fichaje estrella para un Modena que sueña con el ascenso a la Serie A. Andrea Belotti es nuevo jugador del equipo de la Emilia-Romaña. El delantero, que hizo 26 goles en 35 partidos con el Torino en la Serie A 2026-17, convirtiéndose en uno de los arietes más cotizados del fútbol europeo en aquel momento, buscará relanzar su carrera en la categoría de plata del 'Calcio'. "El Modena FC anuncia que ha adquirido el rendimiento deportivo de Andrea Belotti, quien ha firmado un contrato hasta el 30 de junio de 2027 y ha elegido la camiseta número 11", publicaban en su pagína web desde el Modena. A sus 32 años y con más de 180 goles como profesional a su espalda, Belotti viene de jugar la pasada temporada en el Cagliari: hizo dos goles en ocho partidos antes de lesionarse. Desde que dejó la Roma había militado en Fiorentina, Como y Benfica.

articles.title: Urban Meyer Teases Bryce Underwood 'Intel', Reveals 'Issue' with Michigan QB amid Struggles
articles.summary: Urban Meyer says Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham believes in Bryce Underwood but that the Wolverines quarterback has struggled because he is physically "underdeveloped."
articles.body:
Urban Meyer says Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham believes in Bryce Underwood but that the Wolverines quarterback has struggled because he is physically "underdeveloped."

Meyer discussed what he sees as opinions held by Whittingham, with whom Meyer worked on Utah's coaching staff, after Underwood struggled in Saturday's season-opening win over Western Michigan.

"I have more intel than most, because I'm very close with the Wolverines head coach," Meyer said around the 11:50 mark of the Triple Option podcast with Mark Ingram II and Rob Stone. "He expressed, first of all, he loves Bryce Underwood. A lot of times, you'll coach a player that's just resistant to coaching, that's just a pain in the ass. That's not what's going on there.

"His issue is spatial awareness, going through progressions and then executing, which is a normal progression for a young quarterback."

Meyer went on to reference the changes in Michigan's coaching staff during Underwood's two seasons with the program.

Offensive coordinator Chip Lindsey reportedly served in a dual role coaching quarterbacks last season under Sherrone Moore. Whittingham then hired dedicated quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer Jr. ahead of the 2026 campaign.

"The problem is, he was thrust into a starting environment last year with chaos going on all around him," Meyer said about Underwood. "Someone said he didn't have a quarterback coach... never heard of that, especially when you pay a guy $7 million."

Meyer concluded, "Coach Whit really loves this kid. Says he's got an incredible future. But he's also underdeveloped as far as just physically."

Underwood struggled with turnover chances and threw an interception before leading Michigan to a season-opening win Saturday thanks to a controversial Hail Mary.

Whittingham told reporters after the game Underwood was still the Wolverines' starting quarterback but that his leash as QB1 "not something that's infinite."

"He's a big-time talent with his arm talent and his ability to run, and we're just going to stay the course for right now," Whittingham said Monday. "But again, there does come a time for everybody at some point where you've got to look at maybe an alternative if you're not getting what you need."

Underwood will face a major challenge next weekend as Michigan takes on its first ranked opponent of the season on Saturday against No. 10 Oklahoma. His performance against the Sooners could influence how seriously Whittingham considers turning to true freshman backup quarterback Tommy Carr down the stretch.
